_how: Generated by the rustc-dev probe in `_probe` (build: `rustc +nightly-2026-10-11 --edition 2024 -O probe.rs`; run: `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(rustc +nightly-2026-10-11 --print sysroot)/lib ./probe cases.txt > oracle.json`, cases.txt = `_cases`; then `python3 mkfixture.py <this file>`). Each case parses `src` as `t.rs` (edition `edition`, new_parser_from_source_str, StripTokens::Nothing) and runs the `ops` script against the real Parser; `events` are `<op> => <result>` (`{:#?}` Debug), `stderr` the -Zui-testing human rendering of every emitted diagnostic. `ts` is the TS-side op script for `item_generics` cases (parse_generics + parse_where_clause on the same tokens). Scratch copy: $RUST_TS_DATA/tmp/parser-ptg/probe/.
_probe: // Oracle probe for lane parser-ptg (parser/path.rs, ty.rs, generics.rs): drives the real
// `rustc_parse::parser::Parser` (pinned nightly, rustc-dev) through a small op script per case and
// prints one JSON object per case.
// cases: blocks of `### name`, `ops: op op ..`, optional `ts: ..` (TS-side ops, ignored here),
//        optional `edition: 2015|2018|2021|2024` (default 2024), then the source until the next `###`.
// ops: tok | bump | ty | path:Expr|Pat|Type|Mod | item_generics
//   ty            Parser::parse_ty            -> `Ok({:#?})` or the error is emitted and `Err`
//   item_generics Parser::parse_item          -> `Ok({:#?})` of the fn's `Generics` (where clause
//                 included) or `Err`; only `fn` items (`None`/other items panic)
c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => o.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
